name: OpenMP
listed_description: Set of pragmas designed to allow for easy parallelization of
reason: Specification (implemented by libgomp, LLVM libomp and others), not a single codebase; no first-party numeric comparison against a named baseline reachable. Third-party results found by search (blog n-body pthread vs OpenMP) show OpenMP slower than pthreads, and shootouts such as Taskflow use OpenMP as the baseline. openmp.org not opened (not attempted after other sources showed no first-party numbers).

name: OpenSSL
listed_description: Implementation of the SSL and TLS protocols. Also includes a
reason: OpenSSL is the incumbent baseline others beat. github.com/openssl/openssl README makes no performance claims; github.com/openssl/perftools only compares OpenSSL versions against each other (3.1, 3.0, 1.1.1) and publishes no numbers. Search found only third-party and competitor comparisons (wolfSSL, BoringSSL) where OpenSSL 3.0 is slower; no claim that OpenSSL beats another library.

name: OPIC
listed_description: Object Persistence in C; a revolutionary serialization framework, with matching on-disk and in-memory representations.
reason: README only says regular serialization takes seconds to minutes while OPIC takes few milliseconds and mmap about 0.0005 s, with no named baseline and no measured comparison (directional claim). benchmark/ holds robin_hood and funnel hash-table benches and a malloc bench with no comparison numbers against a recognizable library; funnel_bench_result.txt compares OPIC's own robin_hood and funnel tables. Author blog (idryman.org) and opic.rocks failed to resolve.

name: par
reason: README and the 12 headers read (par_shapes, par_streamlines, par_msquares, par_sprune, par_bluenoise, par_bubbles, par_octasphere, par_camera_control, par_easings, par_easycurl, par_filecache, par_string_blocks) contain no benchmark numbers or named baselines; only 'really fast' remarks in par_bluenoise.h. Author blog posts on prideout.net are EGRESS_BLOCKED.

name: parg
listed_description: A single-file reimplementation of getopt with better defaults.
reason: README makes no performance claim and has no benchmark; project is about API defaults and portability, not speed.

name: PBL
listed_description: Large library of utilities, featuring data structures, among other things
reason: GitHub README only states complexity classes (constant-time hash set/map, log(n) tree) and has no benchmark or named-baseline comparison; src has no bench/perf files. Project site www.mission-base.com is EGRESS_BLOCKED, so its docs were not read.
